section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the hidden matters of Rosh Hashanah become revealed on Sukkos, demonstrating Israel's victory openly.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter is,
for it is written,
"In the covert for the day of our festival,"
that "the day of our festival" refers to the festival of Sukkos, as explained in many places.
And this is "in the covert for the day of our festival,"
that all the matters that were in concealment
(in covering and concealment)
in the days before the day of our festival,
and particularly the matters that were in covering and concealment on Rosh Hashanah
[about which it is said "in the covert," from the language of "on the day of the covert he shall come to his house,"
and it is to this that the verse "Blow the shofar at the new moon" refers
(as an introduction to "in the covert for the day of our festival")],
they are revealed on Sukkos.
And as it is brought in the Midrash,
that on Rosh Hashanah we do not know who is victorious,
but when Israel go out... with their lulavim and esrogim in their hands, we know that Israel are the victors.
And this is,
that on Sukkos it is revealed that "we are the victors,"
and in a manner revealed to all the inhabitants of the world,
to the extent that the entire existence of the world sees that we are the victors.
And even though the victory of Israel already occurred on Rosh Hashanah,
and as the statement of the Midrash,
"What nation is like this nation that knows the character of its God?"
that Israel know that the Holy One, blessed be He, will perform a miracle for them and they will prevail in judgment,
and thus it is a simple matter that on the day of Rosh Hashanah they had a good writing and sealing,
nevertheless, the ultimate intention and perfection is that this victory be in revelation.
And this is accomplished on the festival of Sukkos,
"in the covert for the day of our festival,"
that the victory which was in concealment
(in hiddenness)
on Rosh Hashanah is drawn forth in revelation on the day of our festival,
and through this they come to ultimate perfection.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yom Kippur draws forth the inner aspect of Rosh Hashanah, yet even this remains concealed until Sukkos.
section.t: And behold, Yom Kippur is called "Rosh Hashanah" in Scripture,
as brought in Likkutei Torah.
And in the order of the days, Yom Kippur is on the tenth of the seventh month,
and at the beginning of the month,
on the first of the seventh month, is Rosh Hashanah.
And moreover,
our Sages, of blessed memory, said,
"These are the ten days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,"
meaning that Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are included in those ten days,
(and their content is one matter).
And from this it is understood that on Yom Kippur a particular matter is drawn forth that is related to the drawing down of Rosh Hashanah.
And the matter is,
as explained in Likkutei Torah,
that on Yom Kippur there is the drawing down of the aspect of soul and inwardness,
and since the drawing down in the aspect of inwardness is in an essential matter,
it is understood that also in all other matters, the drawing down of Yom Kippur is in the aspect of inwardness.
However, even this drawing down on Yom Kippur is still in a manner of "in the covert."
And the drawing down in the manner of "we are the victors" and in revelation
[to the extent that it is a revelation in such a manner that through it becomes "the time of our rejoicing,"
for joy is specifically over something that is revealed,
as is known]
is specifically on "the day of our festival"
(the festival of Sukkos),
specifically,
on the fifteenth of the month,
when the moon stands in its fullness,
as explained in many places.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between the shofar blasts of Rosh Hashanah and the sukkah's s'chach, which reveals the concealed drawing down.
section.t: And with this will be understood what we find of a connection between the shofar blast and Sukkos,
and as is known,
that s'chach
[for "all 'sukkah' mentioned in Scripture means s'chach,"
and as the Alter Rebbe explains in the Shulchan Aruch, Hilchos Sukkah,
that nothing is called a sukkah except the s'chach alone.
That is,
not only is the s'chach the essence of the sukkah, but furthermore, in the matter of s'chach is expressed
(gives itself expression)
the entire matter of the sukkah]
has the numerical value of one hundred,
corresponding to the one hundred sounds of the shofar that Israel are accustomed
to blow on Rosh Hashanah.
And the reason for this is as above, since the matter of the sukkah is drawn forth through the shofar blasts of Rosh Hashanah.
For on Rosh Hashanah, the drawing down
(that they draw down through the shofar blasts by means of the one hundred sounds)
is in a manner of "in the covert"
(in hiddenness),
and afterward it comes to revelation on the festival of Sukkos
("for the day of our festival")
in the s'chach of the sukkah.
And likewise is it also regarding Yom Kippur,
for it is known that the s'chach of the sukkah is analogous to the Clouds of Glory
[according to the opinion in the Gemara
that they were Clouds of Glory,
and so it is brought for practical halachah in the Shulchan Aruch of the Alter Rebbe in Hilchos Sukkos at their beginning],
and it is drawn forth from the cloud of the incense of Yom Kippur.
And the explanation of the matter is,
as above, that first comes the drawing down of Rosh Hashanah in the aspect of inwardness on Yom Kippur.
And this drawing down on Yom Kippur is through the matter of the incense, from which it was said, "And the cloud of the incense shall cover the ark cover,"
and more generally, this is through the entire service of the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur in the Holy of Holies.
And from the cloud of the incense on Yom Kippur is subsequently drawn forth the s'chach of the sukkah
(for the sukkah is named for the Clouds of Glory).
